nx_a1_bc_001: Visualise the mechanics before choosing: on stairs with crutches, the injured leg and crutches always travel together, and 'down with the bad' - the strong leg does the lifting, so it leads going up and stays behind going down.
nx_a1_bc_002: For catheter care SATA items, judge each option against the two goals - keep the system closed and keep urine flowing downhill - and reject anything that opens the system or raises the bag above the bladder.
nx_a1_bc_003: Dysphagia options sort themselves by one test: does this protect the airway? Upright positioning, chin-down swallowing and thickened liquids pass; anything that speeds feeding or thins liquids fails.
nx_a1_bc_004: Anchor on the timeline in the stem: an injury 4 hours old is in the acute phase, and acute means cold to limit swelling - heat belongs to the later, stiffness phase.
nx_a1_bc_005: When lifestyle and drug options compete for 'most appropriate', NCLEX rewards the least invasive effective measure first - fibre, fluids and activity precede any laxative.
nx_a1_bc_006: Eliminate options that medicate first: sleep hygiene and comfort measures (back rub, quiet environment, clustering care) come before hypnotics, and 'most appropriate' flags the nonpharmacologic answer.
nx_a1_bc_007: Denture questions are injury-prevention questions: choose the option that protects the appliance (towel or water in the sink, tepid water) and reject hot water and drying out.
nx_a1_bc_008: Transfers move toward strength: place the chair on the client's stronger side and lead with it, so eliminate any option that loads the weak side.
nx_a1_hp_001: Screening-interval questions reward the guideline number, not reasoning from scratch - average risk plus normal colonoscopy is a 10-year interval, and distractors offer the intervals of other tests.
nx_a1_hp_002: Patch teaching hinges on rotation and removal: a new site each day, old patch off before the new one goes on. Options that double up or fix one site are the planted errors.
nx_a1_hp_003: Effective-breastfeeding indicators are OUTPUT measures - wet diapers, audible swallowing, weight trend - so pick objective signs and discard options based on maternal sensation alone.
nx_a1_hp_004: Missed-pill rules scale with the count: two missed actives means take-two-now plus backup contraception for seven days; any option without backup protection understates the risk.
nx_a1_hp_005: The adult activity guideline is 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly plus two strength days - distractors quote pieces of the guideline or inflate it.
nx_a1_hp_006: Lead questions in older housing turn on screening: a blood lead level at 12 months is indicated regardless of symptoms, so the correct statement is proactive testing, not watchful waiting.
nx_a1_hp_007: School-age development questions reward concrete-operational expectations - rule-based games, collections, logical thinking about real objects - and distractors describe the stages on either side.
nx_a1_hp_008: For SATA lifestyle questions, accept every option that is safe, evidence-aligned and nonpharmacologic (layered clothing, fans, avoiding triggers, paced breathing) and reject anything that is a drug in disguise.
nx_a1_ps_001: Restraint rules are time-and-order rules: least restrictive first, a provider order within the required window, never PRN. Any statement normalising convenience use is automatically wrong.
nx_a1_ps_002: With hallucinations, the therapeutic pattern is acknowledge the feeling, present reality gently, and keep the client safe - eliminate options that argue with or play along with the voices.
nx_a1_ps_003: A flashback is a present-tense emergency: ground the client in the here and now with a calm voice and orientation. Options that probe the trauma story during the episode re-traumatise.
nx_a1_ps_004: Anorexia refeeding priorities are physiologic first: supervised meals, gradual intake increases, and monitoring for refeeding syndrome outrank body-image work in the acute phase.
nx_a1_ps_005: CAGE is an acronym question - Cut down, Annoyed, Guilty, Eye-opener - so match the option to a letter and discard quantity/frequency questions, which belong to other tools.
nx_a1_ps_006: Escalating agitation is a safety-first stem: the initial action is calm verbal de-escalation with adequate space, not medication, restraint, or confrontation - those are later steps.
nx_a1_ps_007: Consent across a language barrier requires a professional medical interpreter - options using family members, minors, or written translations alone all fail the legal standard.
nx_a1_ps_008: The picture of ICU delirium calls for nonpharmacologic anchoring first: reorientation, day-night cues, familiar objects, clustered care. Sedating the confusion deepens it.
nx_a2_si_001: Neutropenia SATA items pass or fail on infection exposure: accept meticulous hygiene, dedicated equipment and fresh-food restrictions per policy; reject fresh flowers, rectal thermometers and crowds.
nx_a2_si_002: C. difficile breaks the alcohol-rub habit: spores demand soap and water. When a stem names a spore-former, hand-gel options are the trap.
nx_a2_si_003: A dislodged sealed implant is handled at maximum caution: long forceps into a lead container, never hands. Time-distance-shielding eliminates every option involving direct contact.
nx_a2_si_004: Client identification is a two-identifier rule - name plus birth date against the record - and the room number is never an identifier, which is exactly the distractor offered.
nx_a2_si_005: Home-oxygen teaching fails on any statement tolerating open flame or smoking near the source; the 'needs further teaching' format means you are hunting the unsafe statement, not the correct one.
nx_a2_si_006: Sterile-field questions reduce to the boundaries: below the waist, out of sight, the outer 1-inch edge, and moisture all break sterility - find the option crossing one of those lines.
nx_a2_rr_001: Transfusion SATA: two-nurse verification, baseline vitals, staying with the client for the first 15 minutes, and normal saline only. Any option adding another fluid or skipping verification is wrong.
nx_a2_rr_002: Initial NG placement is confirmed by X-ray - the only definitive method. Auscultation and aspirate pH are monitoring adjuncts, and 'just inserted' is the cue for the radiographic answer.
nx_a2_rr_003: Posterior hip precautions are three prohibitions - no flexion past 90 degrees, no adduction, no internal rotation - so screen each option against the three and keep the ones that respect them.
nx_a2_rr_004: After liver biopsy, position the client on the RIGHT side: the liver is right-sided and body weight compresses the puncture site. Anatomy answers the question before memory does.
nx_a2_rr_005: Immediately before paracentesis, have the client void - an empty bladder is out of the needle's path. 'Immediately before' points to the safety step, not general preparation.
nx_a2_rr_006: Metformin plus iodinated contrast is a hold-the-drug stem: the combination risks lactic acidosis, so the nursing action is verifying the metformin is withheld around the scan per protocol.
nx_a2_pa_001: Raised ICP care is a pressure checklist: head of bed 30 degrees, head midline, quiet environment, and avoid anything that raises intrathoracic or abdominal pressure - judge every option against that physics.
nx_a2_pa_002: An alert hypoglycemic client follows the 15-15 rule: 15 g fast carbohydrate, recheck in 15 minutes. IV dextrose and glucagon options are for clients who cannot swallow.
nx_a2_pa_003: Sudden focal deficit makes time the variable that matters: establish last known well, because every downstream treatment decision hangs on that clock.
nx_a2_pa_004: Vaso-occlusive crisis priorities are the ones that fix the physiology: aggressive analgesia plus hydration and oxygenation. Options that delay opioids or apply cold work against perfusion.
nx_a2_pa_005: Visible thick secretions with distress in a tracheostomy call for suctioning now - assessment already happened in the stem, so re-assessment options are delays dressed as diligence.
nx_a2_pa_006: Restlessness, tachycardia and falling pressure hours after surgery spell hypovolemia until proven otherwise: the answer set is assess-and-escalate for bleeding, not analgesia for agitation.
nx_a2_mc_001: SBAR questions are sorting questions: the R is the recommendation - what you want done. Any option describing background or vitals belongs to another letter.
nx_a2_mc_002: A capacitated adult leaving AMA keeps every right: educate about risks, have the form signed, and never block the door - options implying restraint or security are the traps.
nx_a2_mc_003: Informed refusal is the flip side of informed consent: document the education and honour the decision. Options that escalate to persuade or override disrespect autonomy.
nx_a2_mc_004: Organ-donation stems test role separation: the trained organ-procurement coordinator approaches the family, not the bedside nurse - choose the referral option.
nx_a2_mc_005: Room-assignment questions are infection-logic questions: protect the fresh surgical client from any roommate with active infection or drainage; pick the cleanest pairing, not the most convenient.
nx_a2_mc_006: When the provider insists and the nurse still judges the order unsafe, the sequence is refuse to give it and go up the chain of command - options that administer and document, or silently delay, both fail the client.
nx_a3_ph_001: Statin plus new muscle pain equals possible rhabdomyolysis: hold and report with a CK check. Any option that continues the drug while symptoms are investigated is the trap.
nx_a3_ph_002: Trough means the lowest level, and the lowest point is just before the next dose - schedule language ('30 minutes before') beats vague timing options.
nx_a3_ph_003: IV potassium has one absolute: never push. The correct method is diluted, pump-controlled infusion at protocol rates - any bolus option is instantly wrong.
nx_a3_ph_004: Long-term corticosteroids must taper, never stop: the dangerous statement is the one about quitting abruptly, because adrenal suppression makes sudden cessation a crisis.
nx_a3_ph_005: MAOI questions are tyramine questions: aged, fermented, cured and pickled foods are out. Sort the options by processing, not by food group.
nx_a3_ph_006: Phenytoin toxicity announces itself neurologically - nystagmus and ataxia - while gum hyperplasia is a benign long-term effect; 'most clearly indicates toxicity' points to the cerebellar sign.
nx_a3_ph_007: Vesicant burning at the site is extravasation until proven otherwise: stop the infusion first, leave the catheter for aspiration per protocol - options that keep infusing or pull the line first do harm.
nx_a3_ph_008: Red, warm, tender with a palpable cord is phlebitis: remove the catheter and restart elsewhere. Cord = clot = never irrigate.
nx_a3_ph_009: Beta blockers in diabetes hide the alarm: they blunt tachycardia and tremor, the classic hypoglycemia warnings - the caution is to trust glucose checks and sweating instead.
nx_a3_ph_010: Loop-diuretic monitoring is a potassium story: teach the signs of hypokalemia, daily weights and when to report. Options ignoring electrolytes miss the drug's main hazard.
nx_a3_ph_011: An empty TPN bag with no replacement gets 10% dextrose, not saline and not waiting: the pancreas is still secreting insulin for the expected glucose load, and stopping abruptly invites hypoglycemia.
nx_a3_ph_012: Live vaccines and impaired immunity do not mix: scan the options for pregnancy or immunosuppression - the condition that turns an attenuated organism into a real infection risk.
